claim: The Drosophila melanogaster even-skipped gene has a seven stripe expression pattern that forms during nuclear cycle 14.
source: We used live imaging to visualize the transcriptional dynamics of the Drosophila melanogaster even-skipped gene at single-cell and high-temporal resolution as its seven stripe expression pattern forms
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by the imaging data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Despite being created by five independent enhancers, even-skipped stripes are sculpted by a coupled increase of burst frequency and amplitude.
source: We find that despite being created by the independent activity of five enhancers, even-skipped stripes are sculpted by the same kinetic phenomena: a coupled increase of burst frequency and amplitude.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by the cpHMM inference results shown in Figure 8.

claim: Stripe movement is driven by the exchange of bursting nuclei from the posterior to anterior stripe flanks.
source: By tracking the position and activity of individual nuclei, we show that stripe movement is driven by the exchange of bursting nuclei from the posterior to anterior stripe flanks.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through single-nucleus tracking data shown in Figure 7.

claim: mRNA synthesis occurs in bursts, with promoters switching stochastically between an ON state and an OFF state.
source: Furthermore the transcriptional process that creates these patterns is itself highly dynamic. The classical view of transcription as a switch or a tunable rheostat has been replaced in recent years by the recognition that mRNA synthesis occurs in bursts, with promoters switching stochastically between an ON state where polymerases are loaded and begin elongating, and an OFF state where few or no new transcripts are initiated (Figure 1A; Zenklusen et al., 2008; Golding et al., 2005; Blake et al., 2006; Janicki et al., 2004; Chubb et al., 2006; Yunger et al., 2010; Raj et al., 2006; Lionnet et al., 2011; Muramoto et al., 2012; Little et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2015; Lenstra et al., 2015; Fukaya et al., 2016; Desponds et al., 2016; Hendy et al., 2017; Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by extensive citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The eve stripes are produced through the largely independent activity of five discrete enhancers.
source: The eve stripes are produced through the largely independent activity of five discrete enhancers (Figure 1C) that drive individual stripes (the stripes 1, 2, and 5 enhancers) or pairs of stripes (the stripe 3/7 and stripe 4/6 enhancers) (Harding et al., 1989; Goto et al., 1989; Small et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The eve stripe 2 enhancer is activated in the anterior by Bcd and Hb, and repressed by Gt and Kr.
source: For example, the eve stripe 2 enhancer is activated in the anterior by Bcd and Hb, and repressed by Gt and Kr, ultimately expressing in a stripe of nuclei that fall between the domains occupied by these two repressors (Frasch and Levine, 1987; Small et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Transcriptional bursting is widespread during D. melanogaster development.
source: Transcriptional bursting is widespread during D. melanogaster development (Little et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2015; Bothma et al., 2014; Fukaya et al., 2016; Boettiger and Levine, 2013; Holloway and Spirov, 2017; Zoller et al., 2018; Paré et al., 2009; Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the text with extensive citations to prior work.

claim: The eve stripe 2 transgene is generated by bursts of transcriptional activity in the nuclei that form it.
source: They showed that the stripe is generated by bursts of transcriptional activity in the nuclei that form it, and that the aggregate pattern is highly dynamic, forming and dissipating rapidly during nc14.
evidence: This is stated in the text referring to prior work by Bothma et al., 2014.

claim: All seven eve stripes are sculpted by the elimination of new bursts between stripes, enhancement of bursting across stripes through a coupled increase in kon and r, and refinement and movement of stripe positions by the addition of bursting nuclei along the anterior edge and loss along the posterior edge.
source: We find that all seven eve stripes are sculpted by the same regulatory strategies: the elimination of new bursts between stripes; the enhancement of bursting across stripes through a coupled increase in kon and r; and the refinement and movement of stripe positions by the addition of bursting nuclei along the anterior edge of the stripes and the loss of bursting along their posterior edge.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: A bacterial artificial chromosome containing the D. melanogaster eve gene was modified by replacing the coding region with an array of MS2 stem loops followed by the yellow gene.
source: We used recombineering (Warming et al., 2005) to modify a bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) (Venken et al., 2006) containing the D. melanogaster eve gene and all of its enhancers and regulatory elements (Venken et al., 2009), replacing the coding region with an array of MS2 stem loops followed by the D. melanogaster yellow (y) gene (Figure 1D; Bothma et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: The engineered eve BAC was inserted into chromosome 3L using ΦC31 integrase-mediated recombination.
source: We inserted the engineered BAC into a targeted site on chromosome 3L using ΦC31 integrase-mediated recombination (Fish et al., 2007), and homozygosed the line, which showed no signs of adverse effects of the transgene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental methods.

claim: The temporal and spatial pattern of eve transgene transcription recapitulates the well-characterized dynamics of eve expression.
source: The temporal and spatial pattern of eve transgene transcription recapitulates the well-characterized dynamics of eve expression, most notably formation of the characteristic seven stripes in the late blastoderm (Figure 2; Video 1; Surkova et al., 2008; Fowlkes et al., 2008; Jiang et al., 2015; Ludwig et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2 and Video 1, with citations to prior work.

claim: The BAC reporter construct quantitatively recapitulates the cytoplasmic eve mRNA pattern as measured by FISH.
source: Further, as recently demonstrated in Lammers et al., 2020 this BAC reporter construct quantitatively recapitulates the cytoplasmic eve mRNA pattern as measured by FISH (Lammers et al., 2020; Luengo Hendriks et al., 2006; Lim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Eleven movies were collected in total, with every stripe imaged at least five times.
source: In total, we collected 11 movies (Videos 2–12), with every stripe imaged at least five times (see Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and documented in Table 1.

claim: The polymerase transit time was estimated to be approximately 140 seconds.
source: We arrived at an estimate of 140 s (Figure 4A), consistent with a direct measurement of the rate of polymerase elongation of ~2700 bp/min from Fukaya et al., 2017 and the length of the construct (6,563 bp).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A, with citation to prior work for validation.

claim: DNA replication occurs within an average of 10 minutes for loci in nuclear cycle 14.
source: However, DNA replication occurs within an average of 10 min for loci in nc14 (McKnight and Miller, 1977; Rabinowitz, 1941; Shermoen et al., 2010), meaning that there are actually two sister chromatids with the MS2-containing transgene in every nucleus.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The system can be in one of three distinct states: OFF, one promoter ON, and two promoters ON.
source: Thus we model the locus as having two promoters, which implies that the system can be in one of three distinct states: OFF, one promoter ON, and two promoters ON.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: A compound-state hidden Markov Model (cpHMM) was developed to estimate global parameters kon, koff, and r for a set of traces.
source: To solve this problem, we developed a compound-state hidden Markov Model (cpHMM, described in Lammers et al., 2020) that estimates global parameters kon, koff, and r for a set of traces, and allows us to identify the maximum-likelihood promoter state sequence under these parameters for every trace via the Viterbi algorithm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the analytical method.

claim: Across all seven stripes, the model infers approximate kon and koff values of 0.60 events per minute and an r of 67 AU per minute.
source: Across all seven stripes, the model infers approximate kon koff values of 0.60 events per minute and an r of 67 AU per minute.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an outcome of the cpHMM inference.

claim: A Gaussian mixture model was used to cluster bursting nuclei in each movie based on their x and y positions in the image.
source: To address these challenges, we used a Gaussian mixture model to cluster bursting nuclei in each movie in a series of overlapping six-minute time windows based on their x and y positions in the image (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: There is an almost complete lack of observable transcriptional bursts in the regions between stripes from 25 minutes into nuclear cycle 14.
source: The most striking feature is the almost complete lack of observable transcriptional bursts in the regions between stripes from 25 min into nc14, with the exception of the 5–6 interstripe which is discussed below (note that this is not an artifact of the movie alignment and orientation process, as this effect is seen clearly in individual movies).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and visible in Figure 6.

claim: Stripes are defined by sharp spatial boundaries, with the transition between the low-bursting state and the frequently bursting state occurring from one column of nuclei to the next.
source: Stripes are defined by sharp spatial boundaries, with the transition between the low-bursting (quiescent) state and the frequently bursting (active) state occurring from one column of nuclei to the next (Figure 6), consistent with the classical descriptions of eve stripe patterns (Small et al., 1991; Frasch and Levine, 1987; Fujioka et al., 1999; Small et al., 1992; Warrior and Levine, 1990; Clyde et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6 and citations to prior work.

claim: Most of the nuclei that ultimately form the interstripe were never detected to burst at any point in nuclear cycle 14.
source: The first feature we noticed was that most of the nuclei that ultimately form the interstripe were never detected to burst at any point in nc14 (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Essentially every nucleus within each stripe bursts at some point during nuclear cycle 14.
source: With the exception of the 5–6 interstripe, these never-ON nuclei effectively form the boundaries between stripes, as essentially every nucleus within each stripe bursts at some point during nc14 (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Stripe seven moves anteriorly at a velocity of approximately one percent of embryo length every three minutes.
source: This leads to a net overall anterior movement of the stripe, akin to treadmilling, at a velocity of approximately one percent of embryo length every three minutes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of nuclear tracking data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Stripe movement is associated with the dynamic switching of nuclei between active and quiescent states, not just with the movement of nuclei themselves.
source: Hence, stripe movement is associated with the dynamic switching of nuclei between active and quiescent states, and not just with the movement of nuclei themselves.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: kon is very strongly regulated as a function of average fluorescence in a consistent manner across stripes.
source: Our inference shows that kon is very strongly regulated as a function of average fluorescence in a consistent manner across stripes (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Only a weak drop in koff is observed as a function of average fluorescence.
source: In contrast, only a weak drop in koff is observed (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: r features a strong upregulation as a function of average fluorescence across stripes.
source: Finally, r also featured a strong upregulation as a function of average fluorescence across stripes (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: While there is a subtle downregulation of koff within stripes, kon and r are significantly upregulated in the center of each stripe.
source: Specifically, while there is a subtle downregulation of koff within stripes, kon and r are significantly upregulated in the center of each stripe.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The five eve enhancers employ a common regulatory strategy for modulating the fluorescence output of nuclei to create a stripe: decreasing burst separation and increasing burst amplitude with a constant burst duration.
source: Thus, not only do the five eve enhancers employ a common regulatory strategy for modulating the fluorescence output of nuclei to create a stripe, decreasing burst separation and increasing burst amplitude with a constant burst duration, the precise quantitative relationship among these bursting parameters is maintained across a wide range of molecular inputs and fluorescence outputs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the bursting parameter analysis.

claim: The connection between the stripe enhancers is that they realize patterns through the same control of transcriptional bursting.
source: We have now shown that the connection between the stripe enhancers is more than just that they produce the same kind of pattern: they realize these patterns through the same control of transcriptional bursting.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a primary conclusion.

claim: Many of the key features of eve stripe regulation involve the modulation of kon and r in concert.
source: Although, in principle, complex patterns of transcription could be generated by the independent regulation of kon, koff or r, many of the key features of eve stripe regulation we observe here involve the modulation of kon and r in concert.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the results shown in Figure 8.

claim: There may be a single molecular pathway via which eve transcriptional bursting is regulated, with enhancers having access to only a single tunable parameter.
source: The most straightforward explanation for this shared mode of bursting control is that there is a single molecular pathway via which eve transcriptional bursting is regulated, with enhancers essentially having access to only a single tunable parameter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculative explanation.

claim: The fraction of nuclei that engage in transcription at any point in the nuclear cycle is higher in stripe centers than in interstripes.
source: In addition to this modulation of bursting, the fraction of nuclei that engage in transcription at any point in the nuclear cycle is higher in stripe centers than in interstripes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on observations from Figure 7.

claim: Expression flow dominates the anterior shift of the eve stripes, especially in the posterior.
source: While Keränen et al., 2006 concluded that the relative contributions of these two forces were roughly equal, our data suggest that, especially in the posterior, expression flow dominates the anterior shift of the eve stripes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on analysis of nuclear tracking data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A typical nucleus in stripe seven moves around one percent of embryo length in the final 25 minutes of nuclear cycle 14.
source: A typical nucleus in stripe seven moves around one percent of embryo length in the final 25 min of nc14.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on analysis of nuclear tracking data.

claim: Stripe seven moves around five percent of embryo length during the final 25 minutes of nuclear cycle 14.
source: The stripe, however, moves around five percent of embryo length during that time (see Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: Nuclei transition from low activity in the anterior interstripe to high activity in the stripe, from high activity in the stripe to low activity off the posterior flank of eve expression.
source: We see nuclei transition from low activity in the anterior interstripe to high activity in the stripe, from high activity in the stripe to low activity off the posterior flank of eve expression, and in some cases both.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on analysis of nuclear tracking data.

claim: The transcriptional output of eve is a rapidly changing function of time and space, and at no point does eve approach anything remotely like a steady state.
source: But, as some earlier work emphasized (Janssens et al., 2006), and we have directly visualized here, the transcriptional output of eve, rather than a single 'pattern' is a rapidly changing function of time and space: it is dynamic at many time scales and across space and nuclear positions. Indeed, at no point does eve approach anything even remotely like a steady state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the live imaging data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Eve transcription begins approximately five minutes after the onset of anaphase during nuclear cycle 14.
source: During nc14, we first observe eve transcription beginning approximately five minutes after the onset of anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data.

claim: The initial transcription covers a broad swath of the embryo, from around 25 to 75% egg-length.
source: The initial transcription covers a broad swath of the embryo, from around 25 to 75% egg-length, with the highest activity in two domains roughly centered in the anterior and posterior halves of the embryo, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The full seven stripe pattern is not fully formed until around 25 minutes into nuclear cycle 14.
source: Although the full seven stripe pattern is not fully formed until around 25 min, the three anterior-most stripes are already apparent as locally high areas of fluorescence intensity as early as 10 min.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Stripe 5 appears as a distinct stripe last, emerging in an area of low transcriptional activity left behind following the splitting of stripes 4 and 6.
source: Stripe 5 appears as a distinct stripe last, emerging in an area of low transcriptional activity left behind following the splitting of stripes 4 and 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The stripes persist for the remainder of nuclear cycle 14, gradually increasing in fluorescence intensity until they reach a peak at around 35 minutes into nuclear cycle 14.
source: The stripes persist for the remainder of nc14, gradually increasing in fluorescence intensity until they reach a peak at around 35 min into nc14.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The positions of stripes 1–3 along the anterior-posterior axis are largely stable after they form.
source: The positions of stripes 1–3 along the anterior-posterior (AP) axis are largely stable after they form, while stripes 4–6 show small anterior shifts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Stripe 7 makes a dramatic movement towards the anterior, moving approximately 8% of egg-length, or around 40 μm from its initial location.
source: Stripe 7 makes a more dramatic movement towards the anterior, moving approximately 8% of egg-length, or around 40 μm from its initial location.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The fluorescence traces from individual nuclei show clear hallmarks of transcriptional bursting, with apparent stochastic fluctuations between states with low and high fluorescence output.
source: As expected, the fluorescence traces from individual nuclei show clear hallmarks of transcriptional bursting, with apparent stochastic fluctuations between states with low and high fluorescence output (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Bursting is modeled as a simple Markovian process in which a promoter switches stochastically between an OFF and an ON state with rates kon and koff.
source: Following previous work in the field (Golding et al., 2005; Chubb et al., 2006; Zenklusen et al., 2008; Lionnet et al., 2011; Muramoto et al., 2012; Little et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2015; Lenstra et al., 2015; Fukaya et al., 2016; Desponds et al., 2016; Hendy et al., 2017; Zoller et al., 2018; Bothma et al., 2014; Paré et al., 2009; Lim et al., 2018), we model bursting as a simple Markovian process in which a promoter switches stochastically between an OFF and an ON state with rates kon and koff.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with extensive citations to prior work.

claim: When the promoter is in the ON state, it loads polymerases continuously with a constant rate r.
source: When the promoter is in the ON state, we assume it loads polymerases continuously with a constant rate r (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The polymerase transit time estimate of 140 seconds is consistent with a direct measurement of the rate of polymerase elongation of ~2700 bp/min and the length of the construct (6,563 bp).
source: We arrived at an estimate of 140 s (Figure 4A), consistent with a direct measurement of the rate of polymerase elongation of ~2700 bp/min from Fukaya et al., 2017 and the length of the construct (6,563 bp).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work for validation.

claim: The MS2 BAC is heterozygous in the imaged embryos, contributed only by the father.
source: In the embryos we imaged here, the MS2 BAC is heterozygous, contributed only by the father, while the mother contributes the MCP-GFP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental setup.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion prevents discrimination of both copies of the transgene in general.
source: Because of sister chromatid cohesion, we cannot, in general, discriminate both copies (Fung et al., 1998; Wilkie et al., 1999; Little et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The cpHMM allows shifting the focus in the analysis of individual traces from fluorescence to the instantaneous promoter state.
source: And second, by providing a means to fit a sequence of ON and OFF states to the data from each nucleus, the cpHMM allows us to shift the focus in the analysis of individual traces from fluorescence, which only indirectly reflects the temporal behavior of a promoter, to the instantaneous promoter state (Figure 4D–F; see also Supplementary file 1 which the inferred promoter state for each nucleus at every time point and the corresponding modeled fluorescence intensity, and Videos 13–23).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4D-F and supplementary materials.

claim: The clustering reliably separates nuclei into individual stripes.
source: This clustering reliably separates nuclei into individual stripes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the stripe assignment method.

claim: The stripe assignment is invariant over bootstrapping of movies.
source: The stripe assignment is invariant over bootstrapping of movies, and the standard deviation of the AP displacement over bootstrapping of movies is 0.16% of embryo length.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the robustness of the stripe assignment method.

claim: The data represent a kinetic fingerprint of stripe formation: a record of every transcriptional burst that occurred during the formation of eve stripes in these embryos.
source: Collectively these data represent an easy way to visualize and interpret kinetic fingerprint of stripe formation: a record of every transcriptional burst that occurred during the formation of eve stripes in these embryos (Figure 6; Video 24).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6 and Video 24.

claim: All of the interstripe regions, save that between stripes 6 and 7, form in regions where there was appreciable bursting early in nuclear cycle 14 that disappears at around 25 minutes.
source: They also have sharp temporal boundaries: all of the interstripe regions, save that between stripes 6 and 7, form in regions where there was appreciable bursting early in nc14 that disappears at around 25 min into the nuclear cycle (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6.

claim: The contrast in bursting history between stripes and interstripes is less pronounced in the posterior.
source: The contrast in bursting history between stripes and interstripes is less pronounced in the posterior, where there are fewer such never-ON nuclei in the interstripe region (Figure 7B, notice the lower density of red single-nuclei tracks corresponding to never-ON nuclei).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: No nuclei remain a part of stripe seven for the entirety of the 25 minute period shown in Figure 7C.
source: Although the stripe is clearly present throughout this period, no nuclei remain a part of the stripe for the entirety of this 25 min period.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Nuclei at the posterior edge of stripe seven shift from an active state to a quiescent state as time progresses.
source: As time progresses, nuclei at the posterior edge of stripe seven shift from an active state, in which the promoter stochastically alternates between the ON and OFF transcriptional states, to a quiescent state in which we observe no appreciable bursting.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Nuclei just off the anterior edge of stripe seven switch from a quiescent to an active state at roughly the same rate as posterior nuclei become quiescent.
source: In contrast, nuclei just off the anterior edge of the stripe switch from a quiescent to an active state at roughly the same rate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The other stripes exhibit smaller and varied anterior shifts consistent with Lim et al., 2018.
source: Consistent with Lim et al., 2018, the other stripes exhibit smaller and varied anterior shifts (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), but in every case the shift is associated with a similar coupled gain of active nuclei along the anterior edge and loss along the posterior edge.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: For all seven stripes there is a clear spatial pattern, with nuclei along the anterior edge of the stripe entering a bursting state and nuclei along the posterior edge becoming quiescent.
source: For all seven stripes there is a clear spatial pattern, with nuclei along the anterior edge of the stripe entering a bursting state and nuclei along the posterior edge becoming quiescent, indicating a movement of stripes relative to nuclei.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Individual MS2 traces have too few time points to allow for accurate cpHMM inference of burst parameters at the single trace level.
source: Ideally, we would like to have a measure of the bursting parameters governing the behavior of every nucleus. However, individual MS2 traces have too few time points to allow for accurate cpHMM inference of burst parameters at the single trace level.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section explaining the rationale for binning nuclei.

claim: Each stripe contains nuclei with a relatively wide range of average fluorescence values.
source: As shown in Figure 8D, each stripe contains nuclei with a relatively wide range of average fluorescence values.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8D.

claim: The variation in bursting parameters observed as a function of average fluorescence largely echoes the modulation of fluorescence in space.
source: We find that the variation in bursting parameters observed as a function of average fluorescence largely echoes the modulation of fluorescence in space (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8E.

claim: The precise quantitative relationship among bursting parameters is maintained across a wide range of molecular inputs and fluorescence outputs.
source: Thus, not only do the five eve enhancers employ a common regulatory strategy for modulating the fluorescence output of nuclei to create a stripe, decreasing burst separation and increasing burst amplitude with a constant burst duration, the precise quantitative relationship among these bursting parameters is maintained across a wide range of molecular inputs and fluorescence outputs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the bursting parameter analysis.

claim: What appears to be a regular, repeating pattern of nearly identical stripes is created by the largely independent activity of five separate enhancers responding to different combinations of activators and repressors.
source: The most remarkable aspect of eve regulation is that what appears to be a regular, repeating pattern of nearly identical stripes is created by the largely independent activity of five separate enhancers responding to different combinations of activators and repressors (Fujioka et al., 1999; Fujioka et al., 1995; Small et al., 1991; Arnosti et al., 1996; Small et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: Whether the single tunable parameter is determined by the gene through the promoter sequence, or whether it reflects some broad common property of gene regulation, remains an open question.
source: Whether this parameter is determined by the gene through, for example, the promoter sequence, or whether this single molecular pathway reflects some broad common property of gene regulation, such as constraints on the general transcriptional machinery, remains an open question.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an open question.

claim: The limited data on bursting control available for other genes in the fly suggests that control mechanisms are not ubiquitously the same and that they might be unique to different classes of genes.
source: The limited data on bursting control available for other genes in the fly (Falo-Sanjuan et al., 2019; Fukaya et al., 2016; Zoller et al., 2018) suggests that control mechanisms are not ubiquitously the same and that they might be unique to different classes of genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: The particular bursting control strategy uncovered here might be more robust to fluctuations in transcription factor concentrations or temperature, or provide more precise spatiotemporal gene expression control.
source: The particular bursting control strategy uncovered here might, for example, be more robust to fluctuations in transcription factor concentrations or temperature, or provide more precise spatiotemporal gene expression control (Shelansky and Boeger, 2020; Grah et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculative explanation with citations.

claim: The regulation of the fraction of active nuclei seems to reside outside of the bursting framework.
source: This regulation of the fraction of active nuclei, also seen in other genes (Garcia et al., 2013), seems to reside outside of the bursting framework.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: The spatial modulation of the window of time over which bursting ensues suggests the presence of multiple and overlapping modes of regulation that go beyond the control of bursting parameters.
source: Such regulation, as well as the spatial modulation of the window of time over which bursting ensues, suggests the presence of multiple and overlapping modes of regulation that go beyond the control of bursting parameters and that can be as relevant for pattern formation (Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: The anterior movement of eve stripes during nuclear cycle 14 has been previously described.
source: The anterior movement of eve stripes during nc14 has been previously described (Keränen et al., 2006; Lim et al., 2018), and proposed to arise from a combination of nuclear movement (nuclear flow) and movement in the pattern of regulators (expression flow), especially repressors, which are known to shift anteriorly during nc14 as well (Jaeger et al., 2004b; Jaeger et al., 2004a).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: The difference in the amount of the effect attributed to expression flow between this study and Keränen et al. is likely an effect of differences in the data used.
source: The difference in the amount of the effect we and Keränen et al. attribute to expression flow is likely an effect of differences in the data used.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for differences with prior work.

claim: Looking at instantaneous transcription rates versus accumulated mRNA introduces a considerable temporal lag and integration of the transcriptional activity over the life time of eve mRNA.
source: Because we are looking at instantaneous transcription rates while they looked at accumulated mRNA, there is a considerable temporal lag and integration of the transcriptional activity over the life time of eve mRNA in their data, which has the effect of underestimating the extent to which the stripes actually move.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for differences with prior work.

claim: The extent to which nuclear flow by itself would be expected to shift output patterns measured as a function of position in the embryo is unclear.
source: We also note that the extent to which nuclear flow by itself would be expected to shift output patterns measured as a function of position in the embryo is unclear, as it would depend on the extent to which the repositioning of regulators drives movement of nuclei (which it is believed to do [Blankenship and Wieschaus, 2001]), and the corresponding effect that nuclear movement has on the positioning of regulators, which remains largely unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: The anterior shift of the stripes of eve as well as fushi tarazu has been proposed to originate, in part, from cross-repression between these two genes.
source: For example, the anterior shift of the stripes of eve as well as fushi tarazu has been proposed to originate, in part, from cross-repression between these two genes (Lim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior work.

claim: Recent advances in the simultaneous monitoring of protein concentration and transcriptional output in living embryos should help answer questions about the temporal relationship between changes in repressor position and transcriptional output.
source: Recent advances in the simultaneous monitoring of protein concentration and transcriptional output in living embryos should help answer this question in the near future (Bothma et al., 2018; Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to recent work.

claim: The tools available to study gene expression so far have tended to emphasize its static features.
source: However, the tools we have had at our disposal to study gene expression so far have tended to emphasize its static features, down to the language we use to describe the transcriptional output of a gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a general observation.

claim: We are at the dawn of a new period in the study of transcription, as new experimental techniques and advanced microscopy allow us to monitor transcriptional regulators and observe their behavior at the single-molecule level.
source: We are at the dawn of a new period in the study of transcription, as new experimental techniques and advanced microscopy allow us to monitor transcriptional regulators, observe their behavior at the single-molecule level, and track the transcriptional output of a gene in living, developing animals.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a general observation about the field.

claim: The 4329 base pair yellow gene is longer than the endogenous eve transcript.
source: The 4329 base pair y gene, which is longer than the endogenous eve transcript, is phenotypically neutral and provides a means to increase the number of RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) molecules loaded onto the gene in order to amplify the signal
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the reporter construct.

claim: The yellow gene is phenotypically neutral.
source: The 4329 base pair y gene, which is longer than the endogenous eve transcript, is phenotypically neutral and provides a means to increase the number of RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) molecules loaded onto the gene in order to amplify the signal
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the reporter construct.

claim: The yellow gene provides a means to increase the number of RNA Polymerase II molecules loaded onto the gene in order to amplify the signal.
source: The 4329 base pair y gene, which is longer than the endogenous eve transcript, is phenotypically neutral and provides a means to increase the number of RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) molecules loaded onto the gene in order to amplify the signal
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the reporter construct.

claim: The homozygosed line showed no signs of adverse effects of the transgene.
source: We inserted the engineered BAC into a targeted site on chromosome 3L using ΦC31 integrase-mediated recombination (Fish et al., 2007), and homozygosed the line, which showed no signs of adverse effects of the transgene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the fly line generation.

claim: The MS2 system exploits the interaction between the phage MS2 coat protein and a short RNA stem loop to fluorescently label nascent transcripts as they are being synthesized.
source: For example, Bothma et al., 2014 utilized the MS2 system, which exploits the interaction between the phage MS2 coat protein (MCP) and a short RNA stem loop to fluorescently label nascent transcripts as they are being synthesized (Bertrand et al., 1998; Garcia et al., 2013; Forrest and Gavis, 2003), to directly visualize and quantify transcription from an eve stripe 2 transgene at single-nucleus resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The result of crossing males carrying the eve::MS2::yellow transgene with females carrying His::RFP and MCP::GFP is the direct visualization and quantification of nascent transcripts at the transgene locus as fluorescent puncta.
source: We crossed males from this line with females carrying transgenes that express in embryos an RFP-labeled histone to visualize nuclei, and an MCP-GFP fusion that binds the MS2 RNA stem loops. The result is the direct visualization and quantification of nascent transcripts at the transgene locus as fluorescent puncta (Garcia et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental setup.

claim: The imaging conditions were determined not to affect normal development as reported by the timing of the nuclear cycles in early development.
source: Following (Bothma et al., 2014; Bothma et al., 2015; Bothma et al., 2018; Lammers et al., 2020), the imaging conditions were determined not to affect normal development as reported by the timing of the nuclear cycles in early development.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations to prior work.

claim: The data contains fluorescence traces from 2961 nuclei at an interpolated time interval of 20 seconds.
source: The resulting data (Supplementary file 1) contains fluorescence traces from 2961 nuclei at an interpolated time interval of 20 s, representative examples of which are shown in Figure 3A.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the processed data.

claim: Early imaging studies described eve as being expressed broadly in nuclear cycle 13 and early nuclear cycle 14 embryos before refining sequentially into four, then seven stripes.
source: Early imaging studies described eve as being expressed broadly in nc13 and early nc14 embryos before refining sequentially into four, then seven stripes (Macdonald et al., 1986; Frasch and Levine, 1987).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Subsequent work with improved labeling and imaging techniques revealed an initial phase with broad domains in the anterior and posterior, followed by the formation of stripes from within these broad domains and, eventually, amplification of the stripe pattern.
source: Subsequent work with improved labeling and imaging techniques (Surkova et al., 2008; Fowlkes et al., 2008) revealed an initial phase with broad domains in the anterior and posterior, followed by the formation of stripes from within these broad domains and, eventually, amplification of the stripe pattern.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The greatest fluorescence signal during the first 25 minutes of nuclear cycle 14 is in the most anterior region of eve transcription, in an area in which stripe one will eventually form.
source: The greatest fluorescence signal during the first 25 min of nc14, when stripes are not yet fully formed, is in the most anterior region of eve transcription, in an area in which stripe one will eventually form.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: By 20 minutes, stripes 1, 2, and 3 have clearly separated from background, stripes 4 and 6 appear to split off from a large posterior domain, and stripe 7 forms de novo in the posterior.
source: By 20 min stripes 1, 2, and 3 have clearly separated from background, stripes 4 and 6 appear to split off from a large posterior domain, and stripe 7 forms de novo in the posterior.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The bursting process is modeled in discrete time steps of Δt = 20 seconds, set by the time resolution of the imaging.
source: We model the bursting process at each promoter in discrete time steps of Δt = 20 s, set by the time resolution of our imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: A promoter that is in the ON state loads Δt x r polymerases, producing a single pulse of fluorescence proportional to Δt x r.
source: A promoter that is in the ON state loads Δt x r polymerases, producing a single pulse of fluorescence proportional to Δt x r (with the proportionality factor determined by the fluorescence of GFP and the fraction of MS2 loops bound by MCP-GFP).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: The fluorescence pulse lasts at the locus for 140 seconds, at which point all polymerase molecules loaded during the original time window have terminated transcribing.
source: This pulse lasts at the locus for 140 s, at which point all polymerase molecules loaded during the original time window have terminated transcribing (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach and illustrated in Figure 4B.

claim: The proportionality factor between polymerase loading and fluorescence is folded into r, altering its units from polymerases loaded per unit time to fluorescence signal produced per unit time.
source: Since we do not calibrate the fluorescence signal to the number of polymerase molecules for this construct, in practice we fold the proportionality factor into r altering its units from polymerases loaded per unit time to fluorescence signal produced per unit time.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: It is still unclear how the sister chromatids influence each other's transcription.
source: As it is still unclear how the sister chromatids influence each other's transcription (McKnight and Miller, 1977; Lammers et al., 2020; Zoller et al., 2018), we make no prior assumptions about the nature or degree of correlations between sister chromatids (though, for illustration purposes, in Figure 4B we entertain the case where sister chromatids transcribe independently).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The cpHMM accomplishes two aims: describing the bursting behavior of any set of nuclei in quantitative terms, and providing a means to fit a sequence of ON and OFF states to the data from each nucleus.
source: The cpHMM thus accomplishes two aims central to treating these data in a more rigorous and biologically meaningful manner. First, it allows us to describe the bursting behavior of any set of nuclei in quantitative terms. Across all seven stripes, the model infers approximate kon koff values of 0.60 events per minute and an r of 67 AU per minute. And second, by providing a means to fit a sequence of ON and OFF states to the data from each nucleus, the cpHMM allows us to shift the focus in the analysis of individual traces from fluorescence, which only indirectly reflects the temporal behavior of a promoter, to the instantaneous promoter state
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the cpHMM method.

claim: The orientation of each stripe to the AP and imaging axes was determined by fitting a line to coordinates of all nuclei assigned to that stripe in each movie.
source: We next determined the orientation of each stripe to the AP and imaging axes by fitting a line to coordinates of all nuclei assigned to that stripe in each movie (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: The known coordinates of the anterior and posterior poles of the embryo are used to convert the image x-axis to AP position.
source: We next use the known coordinates of the anterior and posterior poles of the embryo to convert the image x-axis to AP position, and register the examples of each stripe from different movies by setting the AP position of the center of each stripe at 35 min in nc14 to the mean AP position of all examples of that stripe at 35 min, adjusting the position of the stripe at other time points by the same correction (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 5F.

claim: Nuclei before 25 minutes are assigned and registered based on the stripe position at 25 minutes.
source: As the stripes are not all present until after 25 min in nc14, we assign and register nuclei before that point based on the stripe position at 25 min.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the registration method.

claim: The standard deviation of the AP displacement over bootstrapping of movies is 0.16% of embryo length.
source: The stripe assignment is invariant over bootstrapping of movies, and the standard deviation of the AP displacement over bootstrapping of movies is 0.16% of embryo length.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the robustness of the registration method.

claim: The cpHMM inference was carried over nuclei binned according to their average fluorescence value.
source: We therefore used the cpHMM to infer kon, koff, and r for groups of nuclei binned on their mean fluorescence output and stripe.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the inference approach.

claim: The average fluorescence values for each AP position were calculated together with the corresponding averaged and weighted bursting parameters.
source: In order to reveal the bursting parameters across the AP axis for each stripe, we averaged the single-cell bursting parameters determined in each stripe (Figure 8A–C) weighted by the relative number of nuclei in each fluorescence bin present at each position along the AP axis (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8D and 8E.

claim: The three anterior-most stripes are already apparent as locally high areas of fluorescence intensity as early as 10 minutes.
source: Although the full seven stripe pattern is not fully formed until around 25 min, the three anterior-most stripes are already apparent as locally high areas of fluorescence intensity as early as 10 min.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Stripes 4–6 show small anterior shifts.
source: The positions of stripes 1–3 along the anterior-posterior (AP) axis are largely stable after they form, while stripes 4–6 show small anterior shifts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The autocorrelation method for estimating polymerase transit time is based on the rationale that every increase in signal due to polymerase loading at time t should be accompanied by a corresponding decrease in signal at time t+telong.
source: The rationale for this approach was that every increase in signal due to polymerase loading at time t should be accompanied by a corresponding decrease in signal at time t+telong due to the completion of a transcriptional elongation cycle with a delay equal to the elongation time (Coulon and Larson, 2016; Desponds et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The construct length is 6,563 base pairs.
source: We arrived at an estimate of 140 s (Figure 4A), consistent with a direct measurement of the rate of polymerase elongation of ~2700 bp/min from Fukaya et al., 2017 and the length of the construct (6,563 bp).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The rate of polymerase elongation is approximately 2700 base pairs per minute.
source: We arrived at an estimate of 140 s (Figure 4A), consistent with a direct measurement of the rate of polymerase elongation of ~2700 bp/min from Fukaya et al., 2017 and the length of the construct (6,563 bp).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work.
